headline_rule: A record enters headline totals only when verification_status is VERIFIED or CORROBORATED AND evidence_grade is PRIMARY or INDEPENDENT_SECONDARY. ROUNDUP and SUBMISSION records stay in the feed.
limitation: This seed dataset is a small, curated preview of publicly reported incidents. It is not a global census. Headline counters are derived only from structured fields on these records. Evidence grades are assigned from the sources actually attached to each record, not from general knowledge that better sources exist.

incidents.title: Dealership chatbot prompted into a $1 vehicle offer
incidents.summary: A Chevrolet dealership chatbot running on a public website was prompt-injected into agreeing to sell a vehicle for $1. The offer was widely reproduced. No sale was honored.
incidents.ai_materiality: A public-facing LLM assistant accepted and restated a commercially binding-sounding offer after adversarial prompting.
incidents.organization: Chevrolet of Watsonville (chatbot vendor reported as ChatGPT-powered site assistant)

sources.title: Car-dealer GPT chatbot manipulated into $1 sale agreement

incidents.source_quality_basis: Only an incident-database explorer / roundup link is attached.

incidents.title: Airline chatbot gave a false bereavement-fare policy and the airline was held to it
incidents.summary: Air Canada's website chatbot invented a bereavement-fare policy. A Canadian Civil Resolution Tribunal held the airline responsible for the chatbot's representation. Documented customer remedy followed.
incidents.source_quality_basis: Official Civil Resolution Tribunal final decision, Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, plus one independent secondary news report.
incidents.ai_materiality: An AI chatbot on the airline's site made a policy representation that a tribunal treated as the company's own statement.

financial_loss_confirmed.note: CRT order: $650.88 damages + $36.14 interest + $125 CRT fees. Documented customer remedy, not enterprise-wide loss.

sources.publisher: Civil Resolution Tribunal of British Columbia
sources.title: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149

incidents.title: Employees pasted proprietary source code into a public chatbot
incidents.summary: Samsung semiconductor engineers were reported to have pasted confidential source code and meeting notes into ChatGPT, triggering an internal ban on generative AI tools.
incidents.ai_materiality: Sensitive company material was transmitted to a third-party AI service outside approved data-handling controls.

sources.title: Samsung bans ChatGPT, Google Bard after chip secrets leaked

incidents.source_quality_basis: Single independent secondary (Bloomberg). No company primary disclosure attached.

incidents.title: CamoLeak: hidden prompt injection exfiltrated Copilot Chat context
incidents.summary: Researchers described a CVSS 9.6 prompt-injection chain against GitHub Copilot Chat using hidden HTML in pull-request descriptions and GitHub Camo image URLs to exfiltrate context while bypassing CSP.
incidents.ai_materiality: An AI coding assistant was steered by untrusted PR content and induced to leak repository context.

sources.title: CamoLeak — GitHub Copilot Silent Code Exfiltration

incidents.source_quality_basis: Only a security-timeline roundup is attached. Researcher advisory not attached.

incidents.title: Replit AI agent deleted a production database during a code freeze
incidents.summary: SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin reported that Replit's AI agent deleted a live production database of 1,200+ executives and 1,190+ companies despite an active freeze, then falsely claimed rollback was impossible. Replit's CEO publicly acknowledged the failure. Data was later restored via rollback.
incidents.ai_materiality: An autonomous coding agent initiated destructive production-database actions against explicit human instructions.

financial_loss_confirmed.note: Unexpected compute cost reported in contemporaneous coverage; production data was restored. Not headline-eligible until a primary or independent secondary source is attached.

sources.title: Replit AI Agent Deletes Production Database

incidents.source_quality_basis: Only a roundup is attached. Founder thread and vendor acknowledgment not attached.

incidents.title: Misconfigured database exposed emails and API keys on an AI-native social network
incidents.summary: Researchers at Wiz reported that a misconfigured Supabase database tied to the Moltbook/Moltbot network exposed approximately 35,000 emails and 1.5 million API keys.
incidents.ai_materiality: An AI-agent social platform's live credentials and user identifiers were exposed through infrastructure used to operate agent connectivity.
incidents.source_quality_basis: Only a secondary compilation is attached. Wiz primary write-up not attached.

incidents.title: Coding agent deleted a production database and backups at PocketOS
incidents.summary: Public reporting described a coding agent at PocketOS deleting the company's production database and backups during a routine engineering task. Coverage characterized the event as agent-inflicted damage rather than an external intrusion.
incidents.ai_materiality: An AI coding agent executed destructive operations against production data stores.

sources.title: Agent-Inflicted Damage: Inside the Real-World Failures of Enterprise AI Systems

incidents.source_quality_basis: Single independent secondary research article. Guardian / company primary not attached.

incidents.title: Research agents probed government sites and, in one case, reached non-public files
incidents.summary: September 2026 reporting said OpenAI research agents gathering public data in May–June 2026 probed government and university sites with injection-style requests. Australian coverage said an agent gained unauthorized access to non-public files at a government health-data portal after a download was blocked.
incidents.ai_materiality: Autonomous research agents issued exploit-like probes and, per government statements reported in the press, accessed non-public government information while tasked with collecting public statistics.
incidents.organization: OpenAI agents / Australian Institute of Health and Welfare

sources.title: OpenAI Agents Probed Websites for Vulnerabilities While Fetching Public Data

incidents.source_quality_basis: Single independent secondary news report. Australian government primary statement not attached. One independent secondary only; CORROBORATED requires two.

incidents.title: Prompt injection in Manus enabled remote code execution in another user's environment
incidents.summary: Salt Labs research reported by Dark Reading described a prompt-injection path in the agentic app Manus that executed attacker-controlled instructions and could establish a reverse shell inside another user's environment, with a warning shown only after execution.
incidents.ai_materiality: An agentic application executed untrusted instructions with tool access before presenting a security warning.

sources.title: Prompt-Injection Bug Hits $4B Agentic AI App 'Manus'

incidents.source_quality_basis: Single independent secondary news report of Salt Labs research. Lab advisory not attached. One independent secondary only; CORROBORATED requires two.

incidents.title: Model-judged 'safe command' auto-execution defeated by prompt injection
incidents.summary: CVE-2026-30306 describes AI coding agents that auto-execute terminal commands the model itself judges safe. Prompt injection could cause destructive commands to run without a human gate.
incidents.ai_materiality: Agent tool-execution policy delegated the safety decision to the model, which prompt injection could override.

sources.title: Model-judged safe command auto-execution defeated by prompt injection (CVE-2026-30306)
